data.title: IBM Unveils Its Most Advanced Quantum Computer in Chicago, Marking a Milestone for Illinois's Quantum Future
data.description:
Hosted by the University of Chicago, IBM Quantum System Two is now operational at Hyde Park Labs and will be a prominent fixture of Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP) upon the site's completion.

IBM's first quantum computer in Illinois extends the company's industry and academic partnerships across the state, enabling the Illinois ecosystem and beyond to scale quantum algorithms and applications.

CHICAGO, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- IBM (NYSE: IBM), the University of Chicago, the State of Illinois, and Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP) today unveiled an IBM Quantum System Two in Chicago, IBM's first quantum computer in Illinois and the company's most advanced system available. Initially located at Hyde Park Labs and hosted by the University of Chicago, the system is fueled by IBM Quantum Nighthawk, the most powerful quantum chip IBM has ever built.

Today, organizations across Illinois are already working with IBM to explore how quantum computing can scale to computationally difficult challenges. The new system aims to catalyze the state's robust ecosystem of scientists, universities, national laboratories, startups, and enterprises, many of whom are collaborating with IBM in Chicago within IQMP's National Quantum Algorithm Center (NQAC) to develop the next generation of algorithms and applications. As the anchor system of NQAC, which was established in 2024 by Illinois Governor JB Pritzker with IBM as a leading member, the new quantum computer will ultimately be moved to IQMP, a first-of-its-kind campus in Chicago currently being built to develop and scale quantum technology and microelectronics innovation.

"IBM is proud to deploy our first quantum computer of IQMP — an IBM Quantum System Two. Today, it can deliver scientifically useful results to organizations across the state of Illinois and beyond," said Arvind Krishna, Chairman and CEO, IBM. "As IBM's first quantum computer in Illinois, the system's deployment marks a milestone for Illinois' quantum community and builds on IBM's partnerships across the state as we expand quantum research across academia and industries."

"I want the next generation of breakthroughs to happen in Illinois and the jobs and opportunity that come with them to benefit the people of Illinois," said Governor JB Pritzker. "With the unveiling of IBM's Quantum System Two in Hyde Park, we are giving researchers and businesses the tool to turn big ideas into real-world solutions. With our growing partnership with IBM, we are building an industry that will give Illinoisans more career opportunities and build a future right here at home."

"The presence of IBM's first quantum computer in Illinois, the company's most advanced system available, is a testament to what's possible when partners across government, industry and academia work together toward a shared vision," said Harley Johnson, CEO of the IQMP. "Today reflects the unique strength of Illinois' quantum ecosystem. We're thrilled to see IBM Quantum System Two at Hyde Park Labs while the Park is under construction, and we're more energized than ever to welcome it to the IQMP, where it will anchor the National Quantum Algorithm Center and further establish Illinois as the global destination for quantum innovation."

"The deployment of IBM's Quantum System Two represents the culmination of a years-long partnership that brought together academia, government, and private industry to usher in a new generation of discovery. I am delighted that this machine is being unveiled here in Hyde Park, where our neighbors and community will have a view into the future," said University of Chicago President Paul Alivisatos.

"IBM Quantum System Two brings another critical capability to Illinois' growing quantum ecosystem and showcases the collaboration that makes our state such a draw," said Illinois Economic Development Corporation President and CEO Christy George. "For companies developing quantum technologies and applications, access to advanced computing systems, leading researchers, and industry partners in one place is a powerful advantage. This investment strengthens Illinois' position as a destination for companies looking to innovate, grow, and help shape the future of quantum computing."

This new IBM Quantum System Two advances IBM's mission to bring useful quantum computing to the world and extends the company's commitment to advancing Illinois as a global epicenter for quantum innovation.

Since NQAC's founding, IBM has helped grow the center into a hub within Chicago where industry leaders work side-by-side with IBM researchers to build quantum applications that can scale alongside technical progress in the field. This includes NQAC Grand Challenge participants Deloitte and AbbVie, who are working with IBM and Northwestern University to build quantum molecular simulation approaches for researchers engaging in drug discovery.

Other Grand Challenges participants working with IBM include EPRI and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (U. of I.) to explore how quantum optimization algorithms could lead to more efficient power grids.

Additionally, research institutions and national labs such as Fermilab are working with IBM in Illinois to accelerate high-energy physics research with quantum and advance technologies for distributed quantum computing.

IBM is also teaming with leading universities such as the University of Chicago and U. of I. to push technological progress in quantum computing. For example, IBM and the University of Chicago recently demonstrated quantum advantage over leading classical methods using an approach with guaranteed correctness.

Now, IBM's quantum computing technology is being brought physically into Chicago. Through NQAC, the new quantum computer will empower Illinois' quantum community to develop new algorithms and applications that will translate to real-world impact. And it will serve as a catalyst for developing Illinois' current and future quantum workforce. Earlier this year, IBM announced it would establish the FutureNow Chicago center at the IQMP in partnership with City Colleges of Chicago, to bring 750 jobs to the region across AI, cybersecurity, data science, quantum computing and other technologies.

With the arrival of IBM Quantum System Two, Chicago and the State of Illinois will be cemented as a leading destination for quantum innovation, industrialization, and workforce development.

Supporting Quotes

"IBM's continued partnership and the unveiling of IBM Quantum System Two mark an exciting moment for the industry and our state's quantum ecosystem," said Brad Henderson, CEO of P33. "Deepening collaboration between industry, our universities, national labs, and state government is what sets us apart and further cements Illinois as a global leader in quantum technology."

"We are proud to contribute the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign's expertise and decades of leadership in supercomputing alongside our higher education and corporate partners," said Illinois Chancellor Charles L. Isbell, Jr. "As a public-serving university, Illinois' mission is to advance education, research, and economic opportunity across the state, and we're excited to engage in work that translates the brilliance of Illinois faculty into tangible, real-world impact that affirms the state of Illinois and Chicago as the epicenter of the next generation of technological progress."

"This is a significant milestone in advancing Illinois' quantum economy and turning our state's world-class research capabilities into real-world economic opportunity," said Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity Director Kristin Richards. "Through the State's leadership and strategic investments in quantum, we are building an ecosystem for long-term industry growth, new business investment, and high-quality jobs."

About IBM

IBM is a leading global hybrid cloud and AI, and business services provider, helping clients in more than 175 countries capitalize on insights from their data, streamline business processes, reduce costs and gain the competitive edge in their industries. Thousands of governments and corporate entities in critical infrastructure areas such as financial services, telecommunications and healthcare rely on IBM's hybrid cloud platform and Red Hat OpenShift to affect their digital transformations quickly, efficiently and securely. IBM's breakthrough innovations in AI, quantum computing, industry-specific cloud solutions and business services deliver open and flexible options to our clients. All of this is backed by IBM's legendary commitment to trust, transparency, responsibility, inclusivity and service.

For more information, visit https://research.ibm.com.

data.title: Canadian Gold Resources Announces Non-Brokered Private Placement of Units
data.description:
Dieppe, New Brunswick--(Newsfile Corp. - November 6, 2026) - Canadian Gold Resources Ltd.  ("Canadian Gold" or the "Company") wishes to announce it will be conducting a non-brokered private placement (the "Offering") of up to 20,000,000 units (each, a "Unit") at a price of $0.05 per Unit for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $1,000,000.

Each Unit shall be comprised of one common share (a "Share") and one (1) common share purchase warrant (a "Warrant"). Each Warrant shall entitle the holder to acquire one (1) additional Share at a price of $0.10 per Share for a period of 36 months from the date of issuance.

Proceeds from this Offering will be used by the Company primarily for bulk sampling and exploration at the Company's Lac Arsenault property and other high-grade gold projects in the Gaspé Gold Belt of Quebec and for general working capital.

In connection with the Offering, the Company may pay cash finder's fees and issue non-transferable finder's options to eligible arm's length parties.

Certain insiders of the Company may acquire Units in the Offering. Any participation by insiders in the Private Placement will constitute a "related party transaction" as defined under Multilateral Instrument 61-101 Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101"). The Company expects such participation will be exempt from the formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements of MI 61-101 as the fair market value of the Units subscribed for by the insiders, nor the consideration for the Units paid by such insiders, is expected to exceed 25% of the Company's market capitalization.

All securities issued pursuant to the Offering will be subject to a hold period of four months plus a day from the date of issuance. Closing of the Offering is subject to certain conditions including, but not limited to, the receipt of all necessary regulatory and other approvals, including the approval of the TSX Venture Exchange. Closing may occur in one or more tranches.

This news release does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to sell any of the securities in the United States. The securities have not been and will not be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "U.S. Securities Act") or any state securities laws and may not be offered or sold within the United States or to U.S. Persons unless registered under the U.S. Securities Act and applicable state securities laws or an exemption from such registration is available.

About Canadian Gold Resource Ltd.

Canadian Gold Resources Ltd. is a Canadian exploration company focused on developing high-grade gold projects in the Gaspé Gold Belt of Quebec. The Company targets under-explored, past-producing properties with significant growth potential, leveraging modern exploration techniques to unlock value. With a team of experienced professionals and a commitment to sustainability and community engagement, Canadian Gold is well-positioned to capitalize on opportunities within this historic and promising gold region. data.title: Madhavan Hariharan to take over as Birlasoft CEO
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 6 -- Madhavan Hariharan will take over as Birlasoft Ltd's CEO after the company reported two consecutive years of revenue decline under former chief executive Angan Guha, while peers continued to grow.

Hariharan, previously the chief financial officer of the $3 billion CKA Birla Group, will take over the reins on 8 December. He will replace Guha, who joined the firm as CEO in December 2022.

"Technology is undergoing one of the most significant transformations in its history. As clients rethink their businesses in an AI-driven world, Birlasoft has a unique opportunity to deepen its relevance, strengthen client partnerships and accelerate growth. Madhavan brings a unique combination of strategic vision, operational discipline and deep familiarity with Birlasoft," said Amita Birla, co-chairman of CKA Birla Group.

"His wide leadership experience across the CKA Birla Group, coupled with his proven ability to drive business transformation and long-term value creation, makes him ideally positioned to lead Birlasoft into its next chapter," Birla added.

The leadership change comes as Birlasoft struggled to scale while peers outpaced it during Guha's tenure.

The company's compound annual growth rate (CAGR) stood at 0.15% FY23 and FY26. In comparison, Zensar Technologies Ltd, Sonata Software Ltd, and Firstsource Solutions Ltd saw a CAGR of 2.13%, 9.36%, and 13%, respectively. Sonata Software and Firstsource Solutions even entered Indian IT's $1 billion club during this time.

Birlasoft could not capitalize on the growth momentum of the country's mid-sized IT firms. Companies earning less than $3 billion in revenue have been outperforming their larger peers for the last two years, especially in an uncertain demand environment and the threat of AI eating into their work.

This was compounded by an exodus of senior executives. The company also saw almost half a dozen senior executives leave the firm in the last 24 months, putting a spanner in the works of any possible turnaround after its revenue decline in FY25. The departures included its COO, CFO, CHRO and key business heads.

Guha, meanwhile, is moving to a company that is also struggling to regain its footing.

Less than an hour after Birlasoft announced the exit of CEO Angan Guha, Wipro announced his appointment as the head of one of its largest market units, Americas 2.

The Americas 2 business includes the company's entire business in Canada and the industry sectors in the United States including banking and financial services, energy, manufacturing and resources, capital markets and insurance, and hi-tech. This market unit makes up about a fourth of its business, as of Q2FY27.

Like Birlasoft, Wipro ended the last two years with a full-year revenue decline and the company's September quarter guidance factors in another lacklustre year. The Americas 2 unit was the company's largest cash cow as of two years ago, making up about a third of its revenue. It is now the third-largest of the company's four units.

Guha has his task cut out. He will "focus on strengthening the business and market momentum across BFSI, Energy & Utilities, and Manufacturing, and to accelerate growth, deepen client relationships, and deliver greater value to our clients in the region," said Wipro in a release.

"Angan brings considerable experience in precisely these areas. I believe this is a smart appointment by Srini Pallia, bringing back someone who understands how Wipro operates but has also gained valuable perspective from leading another major services business," said Phil Fersht, chief executive of HFS Research.

With this, Guha will join his former stomping ground, where he spent almost three decades, most recently as the chief executive of its Americas business, which then made up a third of its revenue.

"We are delighted to welcome Angan to Wipro's leadership team," said Srini Pallia, CEO of Wipro, as part of a press release uploaded to the stock exchanges late on Friday. "His experience in driving business growth, combined with his focus on innovation and execution, will be valuable as we strengthen our Americas business," Pallia added.

Guha replaces Suzanne Dann, who left as CEO of Americas 2 in May this year.

data.title: Zomato launches limitless delivery; how the new service works and what it offers - check details here
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 6 -- Food ordering and delivery platform Zomato on Friday rolled out its "Limitless Delivery" feature, allowing customers to order food from their favourite restaurants even if they are located far away from their delivery address.

"People often have favourite restaurants that aren't close to where they live. With Limitless Delivery, customers can now order from restaurants up to 40 km away. It's a simple way to make more of the city's restaurants accessible to more people," Aditya Mangla, the chief executive officer of Zomato, said.

Until now, the Eternal Limited-owned company's app mostly displayed restaurants based on their proximity to the customer's location.

However, the company has not yet clarified whether orders placed through the new feature will attract additional delivery charges or involve longer waiting times. Currently, Zomato gold members get free delivery on orders within 7 km, beyond which extra charges apply.

The actual delivery experience, therefore, may vary depending on the restaurant's location, the distance involved and the applicable delivery charges.

Under the new feature, customers can order from restaurants located up to 40 km away within their city.

This expands the range of dining options available on the app, allowing users to discover restaurants that may have been previously unavailable because of the distance from their delivery address.

For example, a customer living in Gurugram can now order from their preferred restaurant in another part of Delhi-NCR, provided it is available on Zomato.

Customers can access Limitless Delivery in two simple ways:

The company said the feature aims to give customers more choices when ordering food, particularly when their favourite restaurants are located far from their homes. It could also help popular restaurants expand their reach by making them accessible to a wider customer base across the city.

Limitless Delivery is currently live across seven cities in India: Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata, Pune and Hyderabad. People living in these cities can search for the dedicated option on the app's homepage or type their preferred restaurant's name directly on the search bar of the app.

data.title: Braveheart Bio Reports 52-Week HRS/BHB-1893 Data in Obstructive HCM
data.description:
Braveheart Bio reported 52-week Phase 2 extension data showing improvements in exercise capacity and patient-reported outcomes with HRS/BHB-1893 in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

Key Highlights:

  • At Week 52, peak oxygen uptake rose by a mean 2.7 mL/kg/min and KCCQ-CSS increased by 17.3 points from the extension baseline.
  • 79% of patients had a Valsalva LVOT gradient below 30 mmHg at Week 52; 57% ended the study on the 40 mg twice-daily starting dose.
  • The company reported no on-treatment severe or serious adverse events; all treatment-emergent adverse events were mild or moderate.
  • Preclinical and non-obstructive HCM analyses suggested improved diastolic-function measures while preserving systolic function.
  • Braveheart Bio said it planned to discuss a fixed-dose Phase 2b obstructive HCM study, TRUEHEART-HCM, at an investor event.

Original SEC Filing: Braveheart Bio, Inc. [ BRVE ] - 8-K - Nov. 06, 2026

data.title: House of the Week: A 19th-Century Brick Row House in Philadelphia — WSJ
data.description:
By Nancy Keates

Randy Swartz was working as a managing director at Philadelphia's Walnut Street Theatre in the 1970s when he first encountered a 19th-century brick row house.

Then owned by Philly Pops founder Moe Septee, Swartz said the house was the site of legendary parties with entertainment bigwigs.

"I ogled it," says Swartz, 81, currently the founder and artistic director of Philly Cabaret. The house sits on the corner of one of downtown Philadelphia's most iconic streets, which served as the backdrop for the residence of Dan Aykroyd's character, Louis Winthorpe III, in the 1983 film "Trading Places."

Swartz says he bought the townhome for $475,000 in 1996, when housing prices dropped in the city because of high crime rates.

The renovation

Because the house is in a historic district, the facade can't be altered. Shortly after buying it, Swartz spent roughly $250,000 updating the interior, remodeling bathrooms and the primary suite. He also reconfigured the layout, added air conditioning units and reconstructed the roof.

He married renowned psychologist and author Judith Sills in 2015, and she added her own personal touches, such as painting the dining room walls bright blue. The pair spent roughly $25,000 this year redoing the kitchen.

Can't-miss features

The home's location on a corner lot allows for more light than the others on the block.

Reason for selling?

There are many stairs, Swartz says, including a full flight between the first and second floors, half flights to the bedroom suite, the office and the third floor, plus another full flight up to the fourth floor.

The couple is moving to a condo a few blocks away at the Rittenhouse Hotel. "We are planning ahead for the last phase of our lives," says Sills, 72.

What they'll miss

The block's community spirit, Sills says. During the pandemic, neighbors gathered outside for cocktail parties and book groups. On Halloween, thousands of kids walk the block for candy, and people stop by an open house the couple hosts every year.

Swartz says they will also miss their independence. "Here we have absolute freedom," he says. Living in a condo means following rules and having a doorman who is aware of their comings and goings.

What they won't miss

Their new building has valet parking, a nice change from parking themselves, Sills says. Finding someone to shovel snow was getting harder every year, she added.

Market snapshot

The townhouse is one of the few on the block that hasn't had a full-scale renovation, so it is priced below what others have sold for and offers an opportunity for "someone to renovate and create their own vision," says listing agent Alon Seltzer, a principal of the Philadelphia-based Seltzer Group.

The median sales price in Rittenhouse Square and the wider 19103 zip code in September was $500,000, up 16% compared with the same time last year, according to the local multiple listing service. Seltzer says 10 houses between the two blocks spanning 1800 and 2000 Delancey Place have sold since October 2025, with a median sales price of $3.96 million.

data.title: IBM Unveils Its Most Advanced Quantum Computer in Chicago, Marking a Milestone for Illinois's Quantum Future
data.description:
Hosted by the University of Chicago, IBM Quantum System Two is now operational at Hyde Park Labs and will be a prominent fixture of Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP) upon the site's completion.

IBM's first quantum computer in Illinois extends the company's industry and academic partnerships across the state, enabling the Illinois ecosystem and beyond to scale quantum algorithms and applications.

CHICAGO, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- IBM (NYSE: IBM), the University of Chicago, the State of Illinois, and Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP) today unveiled an IBM Quantum System Two in Chicago, IBM's first quantum computer in Illinois and the company's most advanced system available. Initially located at Hyde Park Labs and hosted by the University of Chicago, the system is fueled by IBM Quantum Nighthawk, the most powerful quantum chip IBM has ever built.

Today, organizations across Illinois are already working with IBM to explore how quantum computing can scale to computationally difficult challenges. The new system aims to catalyze the state's robust ecosystem of scientists, universities, national laboratories, startups, and enterprises, many of whom are collaborating with IBM in Chicago within IQMP's National Quantum Algorithm Center (NQAC) to develop the next generation of algorithms and applications. As the anchor system of NQAC, which was established in 2024 by Illinois Governor JB Pritzker with IBM as a leading member, the new quantum computer will ultimately be moved to IQMP, a first-of-its-kind campus in Chicago currently being built to develop and scale quantum technology and microelectronics innovation.

"IBM is proud to deploy our first quantum computer of IQMP — an IBM Quantum System Two. Today, it can deliver scientifically useful results to organizations across the state of Illinois and beyond," said Arvind Krishna, Chairman and CEO, IBM. "As IBM's first quantum computer in Illinois, the system's deployment marks a milestone for Illinois' quantum community and builds on IBM's partnerships across the state as we expand quantum research across academia and industries."

"I want the next generation of breakthroughs to happen in Illinois and the jobs and opportunity that come with them to benefit the people of Illinois," said Governor JB Pritzker. "With the unveiling of IBM's Quantum System Two in Hyde Park, we are giving researchers and businesses the tool to turn big ideas into real-world solutions. With our growing partnership with IBM, we are building an industry that will give Illinoisans more career opportunities and build a future right here at home."

"The presence of IBM's first quantum computer in Illinois, the company's most advanced system available, is a testament to what's possible when partners across government, industry and academia work together toward a shared vision," said Harley Johnson, CEO of the IQMP. "Today reflects the unique strength of Illinois' quantum ecosystem. We're thrilled to see IBM Quantum System Two at Hyde Park Labs while the Park is under construction, and we're more energized than ever to welcome it to the IQMP, where it will anchor the National Quantum Algorithm Center and further establish Illinois as the global destination for quantum innovation."

"The deployment of IBM's Quantum System Two represents the culmination of a years-long partnership that brought together academia, government, and private industry to usher in a new generation of discovery. I am delighted that this machine is being unveiled here in Hyde Park, where our neighbors and community will have a view into the future," said University of Chicago President Paul Alivisatos.

"IBM Quantum System Two brings another critical capability to Illinois' growing quantum ecosystem and showcases the collaboration that makes our state such a draw," said Illinois Economic Development Corporation President and CEO Christy George. "For companies developing quantum technologies and applications, access to advanced computing systems, leading researchers, and industry partners in one place is a powerful advantage. This investment strengthens Illinois' position as a destination for companies looking to innovate, grow, and help shape the future of quantum computing."

This new IBM Quantum System Two advances IBM's mission to bring useful quantum computing to the world and extends the company's commitment to advancing Illinois as a global epicenter for quantum innovation.

Since NQAC's founding, IBM has helped grow the center into a hub within Chicago where industry leaders work side-by-side with IBM researchers to build quantum applications that can scale alongside technical progress in the field. This includes NQAC Grand Challenge participants Deloitte and AbbVie, who are working with IBM and Northwestern University to build quantum molecular simulation approaches for researchers engaging in drug discovery.

Other Grand Challenges participants working with IBM include EPRI and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (U. of I.) to explore how quantum optimization algorithms could lead to more efficient power grids.

Additionally, research institutions and national labs such as Fermilab are working with IBM in Illinois to accelerate high-energy physics research with quantum and advance technologies for distributed quantum computing.

IBM is also teaming with leading universities such as the University of Chicago and U. of I. to push technological progress in quantum computing. For example, IBM and the University of Chicago recently demonstrated quantum advantage over leading classical methods using an approach with guaranteed correctness.

Now, IBM's quantum computing technology is being brought physically into Chicago. Through NQAC, the new quantum computer will empower Illinois' quantum community to develop new algorithms and applications that will translate to real-world impact. And it will serve as a catalyst for developing Illinois' current and future quantum workforce. Earlier this year, IBM announced it would establish the FutureNow Chicago center at the IQMP in partnership with City Colleges of Chicago, to bring 750 jobs to the region across AI, cybersecurity, data science, quantum computing and other technologies.

With the arrival of IBM Quantum System Two, Chicago and the State of Illinois will be cemented as a leading destination for quantum innovation, industrialization, and workforce development.

Supporting Quotes

"IBM's continued partnership and the unveiling of IBM Quantum System Two mark an exciting moment for the industry and our state's quantum ecosystem," said Brad Henderson, CEO of P33. "Deepening collaboration between industry, our universities, national labs, and state government is what sets us apart and further cements Illinois as a global leader in quantum technology."

"We are proud to contribute the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign's expertise and decades of leadership in supercomputing alongside our higher education and corporate partners," said Illinois Chancellor Charles L. Isbell, Jr. "As a public-serving university, Illinois' mission is to advance education, research, and economic opportunity across the state, and we're excited to engage in work that translates the brilliance of Illinois faculty into tangible, real-world impact that affirms the state of Illinois and Chicago as the epicenter of the next generation of technological progress."

"This is a significant milestone in advancing Illinois' quantum economy and turning our state's world-class research capabilities into real-world economic opportunity," said Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity Director Kristin Richards. "Through the State's leadership and strategic investments in quantum, we are building an ecosystem for long-term industry growth, new business investment, and high-quality jobs."

About IBM

IBM is a leading global hybrid cloud and AI, and business services provider, helping clients in more than 175 countries capitalize on insights from their data, streamline business processes, reduce costs and gain the competitive edge in their industries. Thousands of governments and corporate entities in critical infrastructure areas such as financial services, telecommunications and healthcare rely on IBM's hybrid cloud platform and Red Hat OpenShift to affect their digital transformations quickly, efficiently and securely. IBM's breakthrough innovations in AI, quantum computing, industry-specific cloud solutions and business services deliver open and flexible options to our clients. All of this is backed by IBM's legendary commitment to trust, transparency, responsibility, inclusivity and service.

For more information, visit https://research.ibm.com.

Cleveland-Cliffs reached new four-year labor deals with the United Steelworks union across the company's footprint.

The agreements cover about 12,000 union employees across steel plants and mining operations in Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Minnesota and Michigan.

The pacts resolve all United Steelworkers contracts currently up for renewal. They are subject to ratification by local union memberships.

"These agreements recognize their contributions and give us the stability we need to invest, compete and continue strengthening American steelmaking," Cleveland-Cliffs Chief Executive Lourenco Goncalves said.

data.title: Why Micron's Stock Valuation Now Looks Ridiculous — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Adam Clark

Micron Technology stock was already trading at a cheap valuation before it plummeted in Thursday's sharp tech selloff. Now its valuation looks ridiculous — so long as its long-term contracts hold up in a downturn.

The memory-chip company's shares were up 8.3% at $710.91 in early trading on Friday. That's a healthy gain but would only recoup part of its 17% drop on Thursday.

Barron's noted Micron was cheap in early October when it was trading at 6.4 times its projected earnings this fiscal year. At Thursday's closing price, it traded at a fiscal 2027 multiple of just 3.7 times, according to FactSet. That sounds absurd for a company expected to report more than doubled revenue and earnings in its current fiscal year, with continued strong growth forecast the following year.

Of course, the counterargument is that memory-chip companies always look cheap at the peak of their cyclical earnings. With data-center construction potentially set to slow in the wake of Democrat victories in the U.S. midterm elections, the risk is that a downturn in demand for memory for artificial-intelligence servers, which had previously been forecast for 2028 or later, might arrive a lot sooner.

Micron has a safeguard in place. It has agreed long-term take-or-pay contracts covering more than 35% of its forecast revenue through 2030. So long as those hold up, the company's normal cyclicality — where earnings rise and fall sharply along with memory-chip supply-and-demand cycles — should be reduced.

The only issue is that skeptics think those long-term agreements won't hold up in an AI bust, even with close to $32 billion paid in cash deposits. Similar take-or-pay deals reached in other parts of the chip industry during the shortage caused by the Covid pandemic were subsequently renegotiated to preserve friendly relations with customers.

Still, Micron has another card to play. It can start major stock buybacks from Dec. 9 — Barron's previously estimated it could buy back $100 billion of stock in its current fiscal year ending in August 2027, which would be more than 10% of its current equity market value.

UBS analyst Nicolas Gaudois argues that valuations for Micron's peers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics suggest the market is already assuming a downturn in memory prices in 2028. He puts the risk/reward ratio for the two stocks at a 160% upside over the next 12 months versus just a 30% downside.

Micron trades at only a slightly higher valuation to the South Korean companies, suggesting a fairly similar scenario.

data.title: Oil Futures Slide As Market Holds Out Hopes for Middle East Diplomacy — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni and Farhan Rafid

Oil prices posted double-digit losses in the week after President Trump's Republican Party suffered major losses in the midterm elections, increasing expectations that the U.S. will pursue a diplomatic solution to the conflict with Iran.

International benchmark Brent crude for January delivery settled at $98.32 a barrel, practically unchanged from Thursday but down 13% on the week. West Texas Intermediate, the U.S. benchmark, edged up 0.3% to $90.83 for a weekly loss of 13%.

Prices were driven lower by growing hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Middle East conflict following the Democratic sweep of Congress and Trump's acknowledgment that the Iran war contributed to widespread Republican losses.

"Simplistically, we view this as the reversal of substantial risk premium that had accrued across September and October despite resilient Middle East flows and rapidly normalizing global oil balances," Macquarie Group energy strategist Walt Chancellor said in a note.

Risk of escalation "has now given way to a renewed diplomatic push, less hawkish rhetoric from Trump, and apparent Republican introspection about the war in the aftermath of the midterms," he added.

Some analysts see the selloff as likely overdone. Attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz put at risk a sustained recovery in Gulf oil exports, while Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export lane is threatened by Yemen's Houthi militants. Traders also fear a renewed U.S. military escalation, which could trigger Iranian retaliation against economic and civilian infrastructure across the region.

The shift in congressional control could complicate Trump's foreign-policy agenda, potentially making it harder for the administration to secure funding for the war, but any change in Washington's balance of power will take time to translate into policy.

While going down the diplomatic path would give substantial short-term relief for oil markets, issues of distrust "and the grinding nature of diplomacy with Iran" suggest that course could be challenging and ultimately inconclusive, Macquarie's Chancellor said.

In the meantime, major Persian Gulf oil producers continue to offer steep discounts on their crude to offset elevated tanker and freight costs. State oil company Saudi Aramco on Thursday cut the official selling price for December shipments of its Arab Light crude to Asia--the largest market for Middle Eastern oil--by $2 a barrel to a discount of $7 a barrel to the Oman/Dubai benchmark.

Despite continued threats to shipping, the global oil market is showing signs of a return to excess supply as high prices weigh on demand and Middle East oil exports recover, some analysts said.

J.P. Morgan expects supply to have outstripped demand by 1.1 million barrels a day in September, with the surplus widening to 1.4 million barrels a day in October. The bank estimates that oil demand has fallen by 3.3 million barrels a day since the conflict began in late February.

Write to Farhan Rafid at farhan.rafid@wsj.com and Giulia Petroni at giulia.petroni@wsj.com
